title: New Terraform module: opinionated VPC networking for Redwood Private deployments
creator: Aisha Raman
description: Build a reusable, well-documented Terraform module that provisions VPC networking resources required by Redwood Private (VPC/on-prem variants). The module should support creating a new VPC or adopting an existing VPC, and offer opinionated defaults for production readiness: multi-AZ subnet layout (public + private), IGW, highly available NAT Gateways, common AWS VPC Endpoints (S3, ECR, STS, Secrets Manager, CloudWatch Logs) with appropriate endpoint types (Gateway vs Interface), route tables and explicit routing for private subnets, and tagging/ naming conventions used by Redwood. Module must include clear inputs/outputs, example usage, upgrade guidance, and automated tests (unit/acceptance) to validate health checks and endpoint connectivity.
acceptance_criteria: Module creates or adopts a VPC and outputs VPC ID and subnet IDs
Public and private subnet pairs exist across at least 2 AZs by default
IGW attached for public subnet internet egress and NAT Gateways provisioned for private subnet outbound access when enabled
Configurable VPC endpoints created: S3 (gateway), ECR (gateway/interface as appropriate), STS (interface), Secrets Manager (interface), CloudWatch Logs (interface)
Route tables created and associated deterministically; routes validated during tests
Module supports passing in an existing route table / endpoint whitelist and can create new ones when not provided
Terraform plan must be idempotent and CI must run terratest acceptance that verifies endpoint DNS resolution and simple egress from private subnet
Module docs include upgrade/migration steps for breaking changes and a test plan for in-place upgrades
Security review sign-off present before merging into main
design_notes: Opinionated defaults: 2 AZs minimum, private subnets used for Redwood services; public subnets host NAT Gateways and optional bastion/ALBs

Inputs: create_vpc (bool), existing_vpc_id, vpc_cidr, azs (list), public_subnet_cidrs (list), private_subnet_cidrs (list), enable_nat_gateway (bool), nat_per_az (bool), enable_flow_logs (bool), endpoint_map (map) - accept comma-separated strings in module variables docs
Outputs: vpc_id, public_subnet_ids, private_subnet_ids, nat_gateway_ids, route_table_ids, endpoint_ids, security_group_ids
Naming/tags: use redwood:env, redwood:stack, redwood:owner tags to ensure discoverability; resource names stable across runs to avoid replacement unless CIDR/AZ changes

Endpoint policies: allow a module input for endpoint policy JSON for interface endpoints; default to least privilege e.g., restrict S3 access to specific buckets is NOT default (left to higher-level stacks)
Backend/state: recommend remote state in S3 with locking via DynamoDB; CI job will use a dedicated service account with a long-lived role scoped to the test account

Health checks: implement optional post-deploy verification using a small EC2 in private subnet that performs curl/dig to endpoints and posts results to CloudWatch Metrics/Logs; tests run in CI instead of continuous monitoring
IAM considerations: module does not create cross-account roles by default; provide examples for required IAM permissions in README
Upgrade strategy: prefer additive changes; any resource renames must be accompanied by a state migration snippet using 'terraform state mv' in upgrade docs
implementation_steps: 1. Create module skeleton under modules/vpc-networking with variables.tf, outputs.tf, main.tf, versions.tf and README.md
2. Implement VPC create/adopt logic and subnet resource loops for AZs, ensure deterministic ordering
3. Add IGW resource + public route table and associations
4. Implement NAT Gateway provisioning strategy: nat_per_az default true, allocate EIPs per NAT when nat_per_az true
5. Add route table resources for private subnets and ensure routes to NAT Gateways (or IGW for public subnets)
6. Implement VPC endpoints: create gateway endpoints for S3 and DynamoDB if requested; create interface endpoints for ECR, STS, Secrets Manager and CloudWatch Logs with security groups
7. Add optional VPC Flow Logs module integration (CloudWatch or S3) behind feature flag
8. Write examples/complete.tf that demonstrates create_vpc=true and adopt example with existing_vpc_id
9. Add acceptance tests using terratest (Go) and terraform plan unit checks; add GH Actions to run plan and terratest in ephemeral test AWS accounts
10. Create docs: variables, outputs, upgrade notes and state-migration recipes; include sample terraform state mv commands for renamed resources
11. Run internal design review and security review, iterate on feedback
12. Merge and tag module v1.0.0 with CHANGELOG and release notes
testing_plan: Unit: terraform validate and tflint in CI for all PRs
Plan checks: GH Action to run 'terraform plan' with example variables and fail on diffs vs. expected approved plan snapshot where applicable

Acceptance: terratest deploys module to a disposable test account, verifies: VPC exists, subnets across AZs, NAT Gateways exist when enabled, endpoints return DNS records, private-instance can curl https://aws.amazon.com and can access ECR endpoints
Negative tests: adopt_existing_vpc should not delete resources in existing VPC; run drift simulation by changing tag and running plan
Smoke: post-deploy health check run from private subnet EC2 that performs TCP connect to interface endpoint ENIs and writes a pass/fail metric to CloudWatch Logs
rollout_strategy: Publish module to private Terraform registry under redwood/vpc-networking
Canary: enable module in 'sandbox' and 'staging' accounts first via terragrunt stacks; run full acceptance suite
Gradual rollout: after 48h of canary stability, enable in 1-2 smaller customer test accounts for Redwood Private evaluation
In-place upgrades: provide 'terraform state mv' commands for renames; include an explicit migration plan section in README
Rollback: instruct engineers to revert to previous module version and run 'terraform apply' ; CI snapshots will contain last-known-good plan to compare against
